subject: radiology
title: Cupping and Fraying in Rickets, Looser Zones and Metabolic Bone Signs

steps.title: Rickets attacks the growth plate
steps.tx: **Cupping and fraying** widen the growth plate of a growing child: the metaphysis cups inward, its edge frays into brush strokes and the provisional calcification line vanishes because osteoid cannot mineralise without vitamin D driven calcium and phosphate. The pictured wrist films show that widened plate beside the growth plate diagram. Knees, wrists and costochondral junctions, the fastest growing ends, declare the disease first.

steps.title: Rachitic rosary and bowing
steps.tx: **Rachitic rosary** beads the costochondral junctions with swollen unmineralised cartilage, palpable as a row of knobs along the chest, while weight bearing softens femora and tibiae into bow legs. The pictured bone radiograph pairs those limb signs with the wrist changes in one child. Delayed dentition, frontal bossing, hypotonia and a waddling gait complete the bedside picture that the wrist film then confirms in minutes.

steps.title: Healing draws a new white line
steps.tx: **Healing rickets** announces itself with a fresh dense line of provisional calcification appearing at the metaphysis within weeks of vitamin D replacement, separated from the frayed edge by the still widening plate that then narrows back to normal. That returning line is the earliest proof therapy works, preceding clinical and biochemical normalisation. Failure to heal on adequate doses reroutes the diagnosis toward vitamin D dependent or hypophosphataemic resistant forms.

steps.title: Osteomalacia is adult rickets
steps.tx: **Osteomalacia** softens mature bone with the same mineralisation failure, but fused growth plates cannot cup or fray, so adults instead collect Looser zones and lose trabecular sharpness. The pictured osteomalacia set shows those histological and skeletal changes beside bone pain, proximal myopathy and a waddling gait. Alkaline phosphatase rises, calcium and phosphate sag, and vitamin D sits low except in phosphate wasting causes where it misleads.

steps.title: Looser zones are ribbon lucencies
steps.tx: **Looser zones**, also called Milkman lines or pseudofractures, are transverse lucent ribbons crossing bone at right angles to the cortex, bilaterally symmetric at the femoral neck, pubic rami, axillary scapula border and ribs. They are insufficiency cracks through osteoid seams, not true fractures, and they heal with the underlying mineral treatment. A solitary asymmetric lucency with callus is a stress fracture instead, with a training history to match.

steps.title: Resistant rickets keeps phosphate low
steps.tx: **Hypophosphataemic rickets** bows the legs and frays the plates with normal vitamin D and calcium but wasted urinary phosphate, most famously X linked through FGF23 excess. The film looks identical to nutritional rickets, so healing failure on vitamin D plus a low phosphate with high alkaline phosphatase makes the call. Burosumab, the FGF23 antibody, has replaced much of the old phosphate and calcitriol burden in confirmed X linked disease.

steps.title: Scurvy draws opposite lines
steps.tx: **Scurvy** starves collagen instead of mineral, drawing a dense white line of Frankel at the metaphysis with a lucent Trummerfeld zone beneath it, corner fractures and a Wimberger ring around epiphyses. Where rickets loses the calcification line, scurvy thickens it, the cleanest desk split between the two great childhood bone deficiencies. Periosteal haemorrhage lifts painful swellings, gums bleed around teeth, and vitamin C reverses the picture in weeks.

steps.title: Metaphyseal lines of poisoning and therapy
steps.tx: **Dense metaphyseal lines** also record lead poisoning, healed rickets and bisphosphonate cycles as zebra stripes counting treatment courses in osteogenesis imperfecta. Lead lines need remodelling failure over months in a growing child and travel with abdominal pain, anaemia and a lead source history. Reading any dense line therefore asks three questions: growing or grown, single insult or repeated cycles, and deficiency healing or poison deposited.

Lead lines travel with abdominal pain, anaemia and a lead source history. Reading any dense line asks whether bone is growing, and whether cycles repeat.
